title: secp256k1-ecdlp: deterministic negation-map BSGS with a complete cold-work ledger

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x. The deterministic baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md keys its table by x-coordinate (negation map), uses m=2^127 records, stride 2m-1 and h=2^127+1 giant iterations, covers exactly 2^255+2^127-1 scalars and therefore succeeds with probability strictly above 1/2 (hence at least 0.39), using less than 2^145 total target-group-operation equivalents at the protected C=1000 instructions per equivalent, including preprocessing, routed memory access, sorting, failure paths and verification. Every point step is charged as a complete affine addition with its own inversion (H=0). Preprocessing is less than 2^145 equivalents and is included in total work; peak memory is less than 2^150 bytes; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. There is no heuristic, randomness, retry or quantum step. This is an analytic conservative accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the signed-window negation-map BSGS coverage and sign logic on small additive groups and on small prime-order j=0 curves y^2=x^3+7 with real x-coordinate keys. Finite scope only; does not establish production cost or security.
